title: Nightshift Incident Playbook and Customer Briefs (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, compact runbook intended for nightshift/on-call SREs to manage customer communications during service degradation incidents. It combines short, copyable templates for external updates (status page, customer email), internal bridge starters, and a war-room checklist focused on rapid, auditable comms.

Scope / When to use:
- Use when the incident has customer-visible impact (errors, elevated latencies, failed requests, or degraded quality).
- Prefer this doc for incidents where a minimal external statement is required within the first 15 minutes.
- For major outages with legal/compliance concerns escalate to Eng Manager and Trust/Security ops per usual escalation flow.

Quick reference (first 10 minutes):
1) Create an incident channel (Slack) and name: incident-<YYYYMMDD>-<short-impact>-<INCID>.
2) Post an initial internal bridge message (copy template A below). Ping oncall-rotations and product leads.
3) Check runbook: collect scope, last deploys, recent config changes, and ingested alerts.
4) If customer-visible, publish a Status Page "Identified" update within 15 minutes, then update every 30 min or when ETA changes.
5) Identify priority enterprise accounts and prepare targeted emails if they are impacted.
6) Start a timeline log (shared doc). Record actions and decisions.

Internal Bridge Starter (copy into Slack channel):
---
Bridge: incident-<DATE>-<INCID_ID>
Severity: S1 / S2 / S3 (choose)
Short summary: <one sentence impact>
Impact window: observed at <HH:MM UTC> — customers experiencing <symptom, percent>
Primary owner: <oncall>
Triage checklist started: yes
Key contacts: eng oncall, infra lead, product owner, trust
Next update: in 15m or when there is material change
---
(Attach timeline doc link and incident tracker link)

Data collection quick commands (examples for reviewers):
- Check GPU-serving pool: kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=hosted -o wide
- Check routing errors: curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/errors?since=15m&service=inference" | jq .counts
- Check queue depth/latency: grafana dashboard quick links in channel

Status Page Templates
Template: Initial Identified Update (public-facing)
---
Title: We are investigating elevated request errors for text generation
What’s happening: We are investigating an issue that is causing elevated 5xx errors for generation and chat APIs in the us-west region. Some requests are returning errors or timing out.
What we know: Impact began at ~<HH:MM UTC>, affecting ~<X%> of requests for model /family
What we’re doing: Engineers are actively investigating the root cause; we have created a dedicated bridge and are rolling back the most recent routing change while collecting logs.
Customer impact: You may see errors or increased latency for generation requests in us-west. Requests may fail with a 502/504.
Workaround: Retry requests with exponential backoff; request routing may succeed from another region.
Next update: We will provide an update within 30 minutes or as soon as we have new information.
---
Template: Update (progress)
---
Title: Engineering update: active mitigation in progress
Summary: We’ve identified increased backend timeouts caused by a degraded cache layer. We are draining one pool and redirecting traffic to healthy capacity while we replace the failing nodes.
What we know: Failure correlates with cache eviction storms following a config change at <time>.
What we’re doing: Traffic has been migrated away from impacted nodes; we are validating responses and monitoring error rate.
Customer impact: Errors are reduced but some customers may still see failures.
ETA: Partial recovery expected within <X> minutes; full recovery TBD.
Next update: In 30 minutes or as conditions change.
---
Template: Resolved
---
Title: Incident resolved: request errors addressed
Summary: The elevated error rate has returned to normal after replacing the affected cache nodes and completing a controlled rollback.
What we did: Rolled back recent routing config, replaced nodes in pool A, verified request success rates and latency.
Customer impact: Services should be operating normally; any cached failures should clear within the next few minutes.
Follow-up: A post-incident review will be posted within 72 hours with timeline and remediation actions.
---

Customer-facing Email (concise, for impacted enterprise accounts)
Subject: Brief outage notice — [Incident <INCID>] — Redwood Inference
Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to let you know that between <start> and <end or ongoing> we observed elevated errors affecting our text generation APIs in <region>. Our team has applied mitigation and traffic has been shifted to healthy capacity; we are monitoring to confirm full recovery.
Impact: <short summary of what their services may have experienced>.
Action taken: <rolled back config / replaced nodes / scaled capacity>.
Next steps: We will follow up with a detailed post-incident report within 72 hours. If you need an immediate account-level call, reply to this email and we will schedule.
Thanks for your patience — 
Redwood Inference Trust & Reliability

Internal Incident Checklist (war-room focused)
- [ ] Confirm severity and owner.
- [ ] Start timeline doc and incident tracker link.
- [ ] Tag affected services and models.
- [ ] Publish initial status page update if customer-visible.
- [ ] Identify top 5 impacted customers; assign an account responder.
- [ ] Collect logs and stack traces; snapshot error rates and qps.
- [ ] Validate whether recent deploys/config changes align with start time.
- [ ] If rollback is considered, get approver from release-engineering.
- [ ] If mitigation involves routing changes, coordinate with netops.
- [ ] Prepare customer email drafts; get product/AM review for enterprise messages.
- [ ] After mitigation, prepare resolved status page and schedule PIR.

Escalation guidance (short):
- If wide geographic impact or >30% total traffic affected -> escalate to Eng Director and Send Exec Ops.
- If legal/regulatory customer impacted (gov, HIPAA, financial) -> notify Security & Compliance immediately.
- If incident persists beyond 2 hours without clear mitigation -> consider declaring Major Incident and open executive bridge.

Post-Incident Review Starter (to populate PIR doc)
- Incident ID: <INCID>
- Timeline (one-line per action with timestamps)
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence collected
- Immediate mitigations and why they worked/didn’t work
- What we could have done faster/differently (comms, instrumentation, rollout controls)
- Action list: owner, description, ETA (fixes, automation, runbook updates)
- Customer communication log: who was notified, template used, follow-ups scheduled

Notes on tone and style for public comms:
- Be factual, brief, and avoid speculative root-cause statements in initial updates.
- Prioritize customer impact and practical mitigations.
- Use plain language for status page; reserve technical details for targeted account emails or PIR.

Appendix: Short examples of short Slack lines for executives
- Exec alert (copy): "INCIDENT <INCID>: Elevated generation errors in us-west affecting ~20% requests. On-call investigating and rollback in progress. Next update in 30m. Owner: Ava M."

Appendix B: Common pitfalls to avoid
- Don’t promise ETAs unless confident. Use windows (e.g., "expected within 1–2 hours")
- Don’t include raw log snippets in public updates. Use sanitized summaries.
- Don’t delay publishing an initial status page update; timeliness matters more than completeness.

Revision notes:
- Drafted for shorter nightshift comms where minimal, repeatable templates reduce cognitive load.
- Intend to sync with product-hosted-api and trust teams to agree on enterprise email wording and escalation thresholds.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether to auto-create a status page stub via the incident bot.
- Finalize enterprise account notification roster and SLA-level routing for targeted emails.
- Run a drill with this doc during next on-call rotation.

End of document.
